chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hammad ibn Abdullah from Abu Basir from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), who said:
When a servant says while in prostration: 'O Allah, O my Lord, O my Master' three times, the Blessed and Exalted responds: 'Here I am, My servant, ask for your need.'

key_terms.حاجتك: Your need - whatever the servant requires from Allah
key_terms.ساجد: One in prostration (sujud) - the closest position to God in prayer
key_terms.لبيك: Here I am - Allah's direct response to the supplicant

ai.seo_question: What supplication should be said in prostration according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that when a worshiper calls upon Allah with three divine appellations while prostrating - 'O Allah, O my Lord, O my Master' - three times, Allah personally responds with 'Here I am, My servant, ask for your need.' This was taught in the context of encouraging intimate supplication during sajdah, the position of closest proximity to God.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us from Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami from `Ali b. al-Hakam from Hammad b. `Abdullah from Abi Basir from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
When a worshiper says whilst in prostration: "O Allah, O Lord, O Master! (ya Allah, ya rabbah, ya sayyidah)" three times, He responds: "Here I am, My servant, ask for your need."
